title: Straw to pellet in six steps
look: Factory line: full-bleed machine footage; a steel conveyor strip along the bottom carries the material from station 1 to 6; a giant step number slams in for each stage.

beats.vo: Loose straw goes in. Hard pellets come out. Here is what happens in between.
beats.visual: Loose straw pile, then hard pellets: before/after wipe. Hook: FROM LOOSE STRAW TO A PELLET.

beats.vo: Step one. Cleaning. Stones and metal are removed.
beats.visual: STEP 1 CLEANING: sorting conveyor; stones and metal icons drop out.

beats.vo: Step two. Drying. Pellets need low moisture to hold together.
beats.visual: STEP 2 DRYING: dryer / sun-drying; a moisture bar falls.

beats.vo: Step three. Grinding. A hammer mill turns the straw into powder.
beats.visual: STEP 3 GRINDING: hammer mill, powder pouring.

beats.vo: Step four. Pressing. Rollers force it through a steel die. Heat and pressure make it bind.
beats.visual: STEP 4 PRESSING: pellets extruding from the die (hero shot).

beats.vo: Step five. Cooling. Hot, soft pellets turn hard.
beats.visual: STEP 5 COOLING: steam rising off fresh pellets.

beats.vo: Step six. Screening and bagging, ready for the buyer.
beats.visual: STEP 6 BAGGING: sacks filled and stacked.

beats.vo: Six steps, and a waste becomes a fuel.
beats.visual: All six stations light up in a row: WASTE → FUEL.

beats.vo: Pellet makers, machinery suppliers and buyers. IndiaBiomass is bringing them together.
beats.visual: Brand line, then the shared finale end cut.

title: A day in the life of an aggregator
look: Clock day: a huge timestamp (5:00 AM → 9:00 PM) leads each scene; the sky colour behind the type shifts from dawn blue to night; a thin progress arc fills like a clock.

beats.vo: Five a.m. An aggregator's day starts with calls. Which farms have harvested. Which balers are free.
beats.visual: 5:00 AM over village sunrise; person on phone at dawn.

beats.vo: Eight a.m. Out on the fields, checking the straw. Wet bales lose value.
beats.visual: 8:00 AM: hands checking straw in the field; chip WET BALES LOSE VALUE.

beats.vo: Eleven a.m. Agreeing terms with farmers, one field at a time.
beats.visual: 11:00 AM: two people agreeing terms in a field.

beats.vo: Two p.m. Arranging trucks. Too few, and bales sit in the rain. Too many, and trucks wait empty.
beats.visual: 2:00 PM: truck / trolley being loaded; split icons TOO FEW / TOO MANY.

beats.vo: Five p.m. Calling buyers. Who needs how much, and who pays on time.
beats.visual: 5:00 PM: evening phone call.

beats.vo: Nine p.m. Planning tomorrow.
beats.visual: 9:00 PM: notebook under a lamp.

beats.vo: Aggregators hold the supply chain together, one call at a time.
beats.visual: Clock completes a full circle; ONE CALL AT A TIME.

beats.vo: IndiaBiomass is building one place for the people who keep India's biomass moving.
beats.visual: Brand line, then the shared finale end cut.

title: Four red flags in a biomass deal
look: Red alert: near-black and signal red; a red flag plants into the frame for each warning, a 1/4–4/4 counter; ends on a big green VERIFY stamp.

beats.vo: Four red flags in any biomass deal.
beats.visual: Dark smoke texture; four red flags drop in a row. Hook: 4 RED FLAGS.

beats.vo: One. No specs in writing. If moisture, ash and heat value are not written down, every dispute is your word against theirs.
beats.visual: FLAG 1 NO SPECS IN WRITING: contract close-up with blank spec lines.

beats.vo: Two. A price far below everyone else. Very cheap fuel often means wet, mixed, or not there at all.
beats.visual: FLAG 2 TOO-CHEAP PRICE: market haggling; price tag slashes down.

beats.vo: Three. Full payment in advance, to someone you have never verified.
beats.visual: FLAG 3 FULL PAYMENT UPFRONT: cash counting; ? over the receiver.

beats.vo: Four. No delivery schedule. Without dates and quantities, a deal is just a conversation.
beats.visual: FLAG 4 NO DELIVERY SCHEDULE: empty warehouse / blank calendar.

beats.vo: One red flag means ask more questions. Two means walk away.
beats.visual: 1 flag = ASK MORE · 2 flags = WALK AWAY (meter).

beats.vo: Trade with people you can verify.
beats.visual: Handshake; green VERIFY stamp.

beats.vo: That is what IndiaBiomass is being built for.
beats.visual: Brand line, then the shared finale end cut.

title: The biomass calendar
look: Year wheel: a 12-month ring sits centre screen and rotates to each season; the active slice glows and its residue photo fills the wheel’s centre.

beats.vo: Biomass has seasons, just like crops.
beats.visual: Seasons timelapse; the wheel draws on. Hook: WHAT’S IN SEASON?

beats.vo: October and November. The paddy harvest in the north. Paddy straw everywhere, and little time.
beats.visual: OCT–NOV slice: paddy harvest (north).

beats.vo: From November, sugar mills start crushing. Bagasse piles up until spring.
beats.visual: NOV–APR slice: sugar mill crushing, bagasse.

beats.vo: Through winter, cotton stalks are cleared from the fields.
beats.visual: WINTER slice: cotton picking / stalks.

beats.vo: February to April. Mustard husk, then wheat straw.
beats.visual: FEB–APR slice: mustard threshing, wheat harvest.

beats.vo: And rice husk comes all year, wherever rice mills run.
beats.visual: ALL YEAR ring: rice mill, rice husk.

beats.vo: Buy in season, and supply is easy. Buy out of season, and you compete for what is left. Plan your year around the calendar.
beats.visual: IN SEASON = EASY · OUT OF SEASON = COMPETE; wheel spins once.

beats.vo: IndiaBiomass will help you see what is available, and where.
beats.visual: Brand line, then the shared finale end cut.

title: One new word: torrefaction
look: Word of the day: a dictionary entry (TOR·RE·FAC·TION, pronunciation, noun) on deep forest, then a before/after roast comparison and three benefit icons that light up.

beats.vo: One word you will hear more often in biomass. Torrefaction.
beats.visual: Dictionary card types out the word as a furnace door opens.

beats.vo: It means roasting biomass at a high temperature, with very little oxygen. Not burning it. Roasting it.
beats.visual: Fire inside a kiln; labels HIGH HEAT · LITTLE OXYGEN · NOT BURNING.

beats.vo: What comes out is dark, dry and brittle. Almost like coal.
beats.visual: Before / after: raw pellet vs dark roasted pellet; ALMOST LIKE COAL.

beats.vo: Why does that matter?
beats.visual: WHY IT MATTERS → three icon slots appear over a lab sample shot.

beats.vo: It packs more heat into every kilo.
beats.visual: Icon 1 lights: MORE HEAT PER KILO (flame) over a coal power plant.

beats.vo: It does not soak up water, so it stores better.
beats.visual: Icon 2: water beads off; rain / droplets on material.

beats.vo: And it grinds easily, which power plants like, because their mills are built for coal.
beats.visual: Icon 3: grinds easily; coal mill / conveyor at a plant.

beats.vo: Torrefaction plants, pellet makers and buyers. IndiaBiomass is bringing them together.
beats.visual: Brand line, then the shared finale end cut.

title: Same morning, two phones
look: Two-screen: the frame is split top/bottom (not left/right), each half with its own clock and person; a gold line joins the halves at the end.

beats.vo: Seven a.m. Two people, two districts apart.
beats.visual: 7:00 AM in both halves; PUNJAB (top) / HARYANA (bottom).

beats.vo: In Punjab, a pellet maker has a warehouse full of stock, and no one to sell to.
beats.visual: Top: warehouse full of stock; chip NO BUYER.

beats.vo: In Haryana, a factory manager needs fuel by Friday, and no one to buy from.
beats.visual: Bottom: factory boiler room; chip NO SUPPLIER.

beats.vo: She calls three traders. He checks old WhatsApp groups. She hears three different prices. He gets no reply.
beats.visual: Top: woman on phone; bottom: man on phone; price chips scatter / NO REPLY.

beats.vo: By evening, his boiler runs short. Her stock is still waiting.
beats.visual: Evening: boiler running short / stock waiting in the rain.

beats.vo: They just never found each other. That is the real gap in India's biomass trade. Not supply. Not demand. The connection.
beats.visual: Halves slide apart: NOT SUPPLY. NOT DEMAND. THE CONNECTION.

beats.vo: IndiaBiomass is building it.
beats.visual: Gold line joins both halves; then the shared finale end cut.

title: You asked
look: Inbox: question cards arrive like messages from the audience; the answer types out under each; Q1/Q2/Q3 tabs at the top.

beats.vo: Three questions people ask us about biomass.
beats.visual: Three question cards stack in. Hook: 3 QUESTIONS WE GET ASKED.

beats.vo: One. Can I sell biomass without a factory? Yes. Many people collect, bale and store crop residue, and supply pellet makers and plants. That is aggregation, a business on its own.
beats.visual: Q1 card; answer YES over bales being collected and stored.

beats.vo: Two. Why does the price change so much? Season, region, quality and distance. Straw is cheap at harvest and costly months later.
beats.visual: Q2 card; four factor chips (SEASON · REGION · QUALITY · DISTANCE) over a mandi.

beats.vo: Three. How do I find buyers outside my district? Today, mostly through contacts and calls. That is exactly the gap we are working on.
beats.visual: Q3 card; answer over a highway; chip THE GAP WE ARE WORKING ON.

beats.vo: Have a question? Drop it in the comments.
beats.visual: Comment box: DROP YOUR QUESTION BELOW.

beats.vo: IndiaBiomass. Connecting India's biomass economy.
beats.visual: Brand line, then the shared finale end cut.

title: Five things you didn’t know
look: Countdown: a huge number (5→1) slams in with a fast punch-zoom on a new shot for every fact; quick cuts and the fastest pacing of the series.

beats.vo: Five things you probably did not know about biomass.
beats.visual: Number wall flickers 1–5. Hook: 5 THINGS YOU DIDN’T KNOW.

beats.vo: One. Many sugar mills run on their own waste, burning bagasse for steam and power.
beats.visual: #5 Sugar mills burn their own bagasse.

beats.vo: Two. Rice husk ash goes into cement and steel making.
beats.visual: #4 Rice husk ash in cement and steel.

beats.vo: Three. Coconut shells become activated carbon, used in water filters.
beats.visual: #3 Coconut shells become activated carbon.

beats.vo: Four. Paddy straw can be turned into compressed biogas. C-B-G plants already run on it.
beats.visual: #2 Paddy straw becomes compressed biogas (CBG).

beats.vo: Five. In the hills, fallen pine needles are pressed into briquettes.
beats.visual: #1 Pine needles pressed into briquettes.

beats.vo: The same residue can go a dozen ways. The question is who needs it, and where.
beats.visual: Five tiles shrink into a grid: A DOZEN WAYS. WHO NEEDS IT, AND WHERE?

beats.vo: IndiaBiomass is building the way to find out.
beats.visual: Brand line, then the shared finale end cut.
